meta.title: tenant-pi architecture
meta.intro: The kit checks your private choices and generates a separate Pi profile. It writes new files, but installs no package, starts no service and stores no credential.

placeholders.pi_bin: the pi command of your npm prefix
placeholders.aliases: the model aliases of the gateway
placeholders.mcp_servers: the MCP servers that you define

views.label: System overview
views.summary: The four places of the kit: the clone, the private directory, the generated profile and the Pi runtime. The kit refuses a target in the live profile.

groups.label: The Pi runtime
groups.sub: one npm package for the user

nodes.label: The manifest
nodes.summary: Each component with its source, pin and status, and the runtime requirements. The public input of the plan. A kit update changes the manifest and never your choices.

nodes.label: Sample overlay
nodes.summary: A synthetic core-only overlay. init-private adapts it to your target.

nodes.label: Private templates
nodes.summary: The templates of the registry, the install log, the accepted-drift list and the Git ignore file of the private directory.

nodes.label: In-tree packages
nodes.summary: The optional modules: packages/tenantext, packages/promptr and packages/openviking-pi. A profile points at them by absolute path, so the clone must stay in its place.

nodes.label: The command line
nodes.summary: The options, the bounded file loader and each action. python3 scripts/tenant_pi.py --help lists the actions.

nodes.label: Offline checks
nodes.summary: You run the unit tests and the publish check after the clone. They need no network and change nothing.

nodes.label: Your overlay
nodes.summary: Your choices: the target, the component selection, the models, the references and the consent. The private input of the plan.

nodes.label: Model registry
nodes.summary: Your evidence that a provider has a model. Only model routes need it. You pass it with --registry.

nodes.label: Module inputs
nodes.summary: The input files of optional modules, for example inputs/mcp-adapter.json. validate, plan and generate read them with --local-dir.

nodes.label: Runtime report
nodes.summary: The saved output of check-runtime: the installed Pi, Node and Python, compared with the pins of the manifest.

nodes.label: Launcher file
nodes.summary: Two lines that start Pi with the target as its profile. generate writes it with --launcher. Mode 0700.

nodes.label: Live baseline
nodes.summary: The entry names, sizes and modification times of the live profile. check-baseline compares the live profile with it.

nodes.label: Install log
nodes.summary: Your record of each install. accepted-drift.md beside it lists the differences that you keep on purpose.

nodes.label: init-private
nodes.summary: Creates the private directory from the templates, mode 0700, with five files and an empty inputs/ directory.

nodes.label: check-runtime
nodes.summary: Starts three --version processes and compares Pi, Node and Python with the pins of the manifest. The Pi probe uses an empty temporary profile.

nodes.label: validate
nodes.summary: Checks the overlay against the manifest, offline. A refusal prints rule: field on standard error and exits with code 2. It never prints a path or a value.

nodes.label: plan (pure)
nodes.summary: Builds the files, the launch line and the readiness gaps in memory. It writes nothing. A command that changes the machine is display text only.

nodes.label: generate (the writer)
nodes.summary: The one function that creates a profile. It creates a new, absent directory or stops. It builds the plan a second time from the record and refuses a difference.

nodes.label: baseline
nodes.summary: baseline records the entry names, sizes and times of one directory. check-baseline then reports unchanged, changed or no_baseline. It opens no file of the directory.

nodes.label: settings.json
nodes.summary: The Pi settings: the core keys, the package entries with filters and the model defaults. Pi can change it later, and compare shows the drift.

nodes.label: choices.json
nodes.summary: The inputs of this profile. They explain each byte of settings.json.

nodes.label: state.json
nodes.summary: The marker and the record of the generation. The list action reads it.

nodes.label: Pi state
nodes.summary: The login, the sessions, the model data and the helper tools. Pi writes them at run time. The kit does not read auth.json.

nodes.label: Pi
nodes.summary: The pi program: one npm package for the user, shared by each profile. The launcher starts it with PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR set to the target.

nodes.label: Model provider
nodes.summary: Pi gets a credential from /login or from a key in the launching shell, never from a file of the kit. The provider answers the model requests.

nodes.label: Live profile
nodes.summary: The profile that a bare pi command opens. The kit refuses a target in it or under it, with the rule under_pi_agent. It stays the fallback until a candidate replaces it.

views.label: Pipeline
views.summary: From two inputs to a running profile. Validate and plan are pure. Only the guarded writer creates files. You run each install command yourself.

nodes.label: The manifest
nodes.summary: The public, reviewed input: components, pins, statuses and the runtime ranges.

nodes.label: init-private
nodes.summary: Creates the private directory from the templates of config/private/ and adapts the sample overlay to the target.

nodes.label: Your overlay
nodes.summary: The private input: your target, the selection, the routes, the references and the consent.

nodes.label: Model registry
nodes.summary: The evidence for a model choice. validate needs it with --registry when modelRoutes names a model.

nodes.label: Module inputs
nodes.summary: The input file of the MCP module. validate, plan and generate need --local-dir for it.

nodes.label: validate
nodes.summary: The rules of the manifest and of the overlay. A refusal prints rule: field and exits with code 2.

nodes.label: components
nodes.summary: Prints the checklist of all components with the recommended set marked. It enables nothing.

nodes.label: check-runtime
nodes.summary: Compares the installed Pi, Node and Python with the pins. Its report goes into the plan with --runtime-report.

nodes.label: check-herdr
nodes.summary: Runs one herdr --version and reports present, missing or unparsed. It installs nothing.

nodes.label: check-wiki-vault
nodes.summary: Reports the personal LLM Wiki vault from lstat calls: present, absent, or a second vault through WIKI_HOME. It opens no file.

nodes.label: plan
nodes.summary: prepare() builds the files, the launch line and the gaps. The plan does not depend on the machine. It writes nothing.

nodes.label: Model routes
nodes.summary: Adds the model roles and routes to the plan: defaultProvider, defaultModel and defaultThinkingLevel.

nodes.label: Memory modules
nodes.summary: Adds the Hermes, LLM Wiki and OpenViking configuration to the plan. Each needs consent in the overlay.

nodes.label: Workflow modules
nodes.summary: Adds the MCP adapter and the question extension to the plan.

nodes.label: Gaps and display lines
nodes.summary: The plan output: each readiness gap, the files, and the commands that change the machine as display text. You read them and run them.

nodes.label: generate
nodes.summary: Writes a new profile into an absent target. It refuses a target under the live profile, inside the clone or inside a wiki vault.

nodes.label: The target
nodes.summary: The new profile: settings.json and the .tenant-pi/ records. Mode 0700 for the directory, 0600 for each file.

nodes.label: Launcher file
nodes.summary: With --launcher, generate also writes the launcher file into the private directory.

nodes.label: Install by hand
nodes.sub: Node, Pi, npm ci, pi install
nodes.summary: You install Node 24, Pi at the pin and the packages of the enabled modules. The kit runs none of these commands.

nodes.label: Launch Pi
nodes.summary: The launcher starts Pi with the target as its profile. You log in with /login inside Pi, or with a key in the shell.

nodes.label: baseline, check-baseline
nodes.summary: Before the launch, record the live profile. After the session, check-baseline shows whether the live profile changed.

nodes.label: results
nodes.summary: Writes INSTALLER_KIT_RESULTS.md at the end of an install, from the overlay, the candidates and a facts file.

nodes.label: pi-update
nodes.summary: detect finds a new npm release. qualify tests an isolated candidate. notes reads the breaking changes. It changes no pin and no profile.

nodes.label: New candidate
nodes.summary: An update is a new target from the same overlay. The old profile stays as the way back.

nodes.label: list
nodes.summary: Lists the candidates under one parent directory from their state.json files. Read-only.

nodes.label: inventory
nodes.summary: Names the packages, extensions, skills and prompts of one profile. Read-only.

nodes.label: compare
nodes.summary: A redacted comparison of two profile directories. It shows the drift that Pi wrote.

nodes.label: carry
nodes.summary: Prints overlay patches from a compare report. You apply the wanted patches. It writes nothing.

views.label: Components
views.summary: The components of config/manifest.json, grouped by kind. Core is always on. Each other component is optional and requires core.

nodes.label: core
nodes.summary: Pi itself at the pin. The only component that is always on. Each other component requires it.

nodes.label: model-routing
nodes.summary: Builtin Pi settings for the default provider, model and thinking level, and the model cycle.
nodes.inputs: roles, optional modelRoutes; --registry when modelRoutes names a model

nodes.label: tenantext
nodes.summary: The base Tenantext extension of the in-tree package.

nodes.label: codex-accounts
nodes.summary: The routing client of the gateway route. It sends model requests to an HTTPS gateway that ends in /v1. Its login route is blocked.

nodes.label: slopscore
nodes.summary: A spend readout by model, role and tool.

nodes.label: context-meter
nodes.summary: Shows the context use of the session. ops-footer needs it.

nodes.label: ops-footer
nodes.summary: A footer with usage readings and health checks. It receives the readings of the usage components.

nodes.label: copilot-usage
nodes.summary: Reads the Copilot quota. It reads login files and environment tokens of the account and sends one to the usage endpoint.

nodes.label: anthropic-usage
nodes.summary: Reads the Claude quota with an active login, read-only. Mode off sends nothing.

nodes.label: doctor
nodes.summary: Checks the setup of the Tenantext extensions and reports on the extensions that are not enabled.

nodes.label: resources
nodes.summary: Manages the resource selections of the profile: toggles in settings.json.

nodes.label: promptr
nodes.summary: The Promptr extension. It needs npm ci and npm run build in packages/promptr before the first start. It keeps state in the profile and in the project.
nodes.inputs: npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build in packages/promptr

nodes.label: generate-task-prompt
nodes.summary: A Promptr skill that writes a task prompt from a packet.

nodes.label: handoff
nodes.summary: A Promptr skill that writes a handoff file from evidence.

nodes.label: openknowledge-project-pages
nodes.summary: A Promptr skill that reads and writes shared project pages through the OpenKnowledge API.

nodes.label: watch-herdr-agents
nodes.summary: A Promptr skill that watches Herdr agent panes. It needs the herdr command.

nodes.label: hermes
nodes.summary: Local memory in the profile: hermes-memory-config.json and runtime memory files. It uses the native module better-sqlite3.
nodes.inputs: memory.hermes; roles.memory when backgroundReview is true

nodes.label: wiki
nodes.summary: LLM Wiki: profile settings and a personal vault outside the target. An existing vault is used as it is.

nodes.label: openviking
nodes.summary: The vendored OpenViking extension. It writes sessions and memories to a separately configured OpenViking server.
nodes.inputs: memory.openviking; npm ci --ignore-scripts in packages/openviking-pi; a server

nodes.label: coordinator-skills
nodes.summary: Skills for a coordinator: grilling, wayfinder, research, prototype, specs and tickets, review, status. They name host tools that the kit does not install.
nodes.inputs: a Gitea tracker for to-spec, to-tickets and wayfinder

nodes.label: knowledge-skills
nodes.summary: Skills for OpenKnowledge and the Open Knowledge Format. The MCP server and the ok command are external tools.
nodes.inputs: the OpenKnowledge MCP server and the ok command

nodes.label: slopscore-pr
nodes.summary: A skill that puts the slopscore block into a pull request.
nodes.inputs: the host tools of the skill

nodes.label: tracker-site
nodes.summary: A skill that builds a tracker brief and site from the repository and its issue tracker.
nodes.inputs: Python 3.11 and Git on PATH; PYTHONPATH set to packages/tenantext

nodes.label: herdr
nodes.summary: The Herdr skill. Agent fan-out goes through it. It does not install the Herdr application.

nodes.label: herdr-relay
nodes.summary: Runs a shell command through a standing worker pane. Optional and off by default.
nodes.inputs: herdr enabled, the herdr tool, Python 3

nodes.label: questions
nodes.summary: The Pi question extension at an exact version. It gives Pi the ask_user_question tool.

nodes.label: mcp
nodes.summary: The MCP adapter with definitions from a private input file. It disables the native Pi MCP and runs in exclusive mode.

nodes.label: Compose seat
nodes.summary: A container, started by Compose, that holds one generated Pi profile for one user and is reached over SSH. Not qualified.

nodes.label: compose-plan
nodes.summary: Turns the answers of the container destination into the overlay, the registry, the two env files and the Compose command lines. Without --write it writes nothing.

edges.label: the private files of the seat

views.label: Development and release
views.summary: The kit is developed in {{dev_repo}}. A reviewed snapshot of the publish set goes to {{mirror}} on {{publication_service}}.

nodes.label: main
nodes.summary: The development history of the kit. It can hold development-only files and notes that never publish.

nodes.label: A change branch
nodes.summary: A change goes on its own branch. The pre-commit hook scans each staged change. The branch merges into main after the checks pass.

nodes.label: Dev-only list
nodes.summary: The optional list of development-only files and directories. It excludes itself. A portable snapshot has neither the list nor its files.

nodes.label: Ignored .local/
nodes.summary: Private client state and the local deny list. Git ignores it, but the ignore rule is not a security or publication control.

nodes.label: Unit tests
nodes.summary: The unit tests of the kit. They include the documentation check and the build check of this architecture file.

nodes.label: Examples
nodes.summary: Checks or regenerates the synthetic examples.

nodes.label: Sample overlay
nodes.summary: Validates config/config.example.json against the manifest.

nodes.label: Publish check
nodes.summary: Checks the reviewed publish set: each tracked file is published, excluded or dev-only; no secret pattern; the public reader rules; the examples.

nodes.label: Public reader rules
nodes.summary: Finds content that a stranger must not get: a tracker reference, a machine path, a host record, a deny-list pattern. A finding never prints the text.

nodes.label: Doc check
nodes.summary: Checks the links, the JSON examples and the CLI names of the published documents. The unit tests run it too.

nodes.label: scan.sh
nodes.summary: Stops a secret or a host value before it goes to a remote. It runs gitleaks with no network and a redacted output. Level fail on portable refs, warn elsewhere.

nodes.label: Host-value lists
nodes.summary: The tracked deny list, the untracked local deny list, the private-address rules, the allow list and the accepted lines.

nodes.label: Git hooks
nodes.summary: pre-commit and pre-merge-commit scan the staged change. pre-push scans the commits that the push sends. A hook fails closed.

nodes.label: Checks workflow
nodes.summary: Runs the offline commands on each push and pull request, with no secret and no package install.

nodes.label: Pi update workflow
nodes.summary: Daily: detects a new Pi release, qualifies it, reads its notes and proposes a pull request.

nodes.label: Update pull request
nodes.summary: A proposed pin move. A person reviews it before it merges. See the pin move guide.

nodes.label: Publish set
nodes.summary: Exact reviewed paths and one directory rule for each in-tree package. Only these files reach the snapshot.

nodes.label: publish_portable.py
nodes.summary: Refuses a dirty tree, runs the four offline checks, builds a tree of the publish set through a temporary index and makes the snapshot commit and tag.

nodes.label: portable branch
nodes.summary: Each snapshot has the previous snapshot as its parent. The history holds snapshots, not the source history.

nodes.label: Snapshot tags
nodes.summary: An annotated tag for each snapshot, with a neutral identity and no signature. The branch and the tag move in one transaction.

nodes.label: Public mirror
nodes.summary: The published copy on {{publication_service}}. It is a snapshot mirror and takes no issues.

nodes.label: Release entry
nodes.summary: A tag can have a release entry with the release notes: the result of each gate and the open gaps.

views.label: Runtime and services
views.summary: What a generated profile talks to at run time. The kit configures references only. It starts no service and writes no endpoint key.

nodes.label: Pi
nodes.summary: The Pi process of the profile. It loads each enabled component as a normal extension or skill through one package entry with a filter.

nodes.label: settings.json
nodes.summary: The package entries and the model defaults that the kit generated.

nodes.label: Profile state
nodes.summary: The login, the sessions and the local memory stores. Host-only: Pi writes them at run time.

nodes.label: Routing client
nodes.summary: The Tenantext routing client. It sends the model requests of the profile to the gateway.

nodes.label: Launch line and key
nodes.summary: TENANTEXT_LITELLM_BASE_URL goes in front of the launch line. TENANTEXT_LITELLM_API_KEY stays in the launching shell. The kit never stores the key.

nodes.label: The gateway
nodes.summary: The gateway route ends at {{gateway}}. The endpoint is HTTPS and ends in /v1. It is a host service, and the kit does not check it.

nodes.label: Model aliases
nodes.summary: The models that the gateway offers: {{aliases}}. The overlay names one for each role, and the registry holds the evidence.

nodes.label: Model provider
nodes.summary: The upstream of the gateway. It answers the model requests.

nodes.label: Hermes memory
nodes.summary: Local memory in the profile. backgroundReview permits independent model calls and needs roles.memory.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki
nodes.summary: A personal wiki of pages that the agent writes and recalls.

nodes.label: Wiki vault
nodes.summary: The vault of the account, outside the target. WIKI_HOME selects another wiki home. The kit refuses a target inside a vault.

nodes.label: OpenViking extension
nodes.summary: The vendored extension. It reads its endpoint and key from OPENVIKING_* variables or ~/.openviking/, never from the kit.

nodes.label: OpenViking server
nodes.summary: The server keeps the sessions and the memories: {{ov_server}}. It needs viking:// home alias support.

nodes.label: MCP adapter
nodes.summary: pi-mcp-adapter with the definitions of the private input file. PI_MCP_CONFIG_MODE=exclusive on the launch line.

nodes.label: Knowledge skills
nodes.summary: Skills that read and write OpenKnowledge projects.

nodes.label: Herdr skill
nodes.summary: Finds, reads and prompts agent panes, and starts new ones.

nodes.label: MCP servers
nodes.summary: The adapter calls {{mcp_servers}}. Tokens can use the keyring of the operating system.

nodes.label: OpenKnowledge
nodes.summary: A markdown knowledge base with an MCP server and the ok command: {{ok_service}}. The kit installs neither.

nodes.label: Herdr application
nodes.summary: A terminal workspace manager for coding agents. A host tool: check-herdr reports it, and the kit does not install it.

nodes.label: Compose seat
nodes.summary: One generated profile in a container. The gateway key reaches the seat account through a file in a tmpfs, never through the image.

nodes.label: SSH login
nodes.summary: Key-only sshd for the one seat account. The login opens a tmux shell with Pi and Herdr.

nodes.label: Test machine
nodes.summary: Optional. You can run a hands-on trial on {{lab_vm}} with a clean account. Never run a trial on the profile of your daily work.

tour.title: Two inputs: the manifest
tour.text: The manifest in the clone is public and reviewed. It names each component, its source, its pin and its status.

tour.title: Two inputs: your overlay
tour.text: Your overlay in the private directory holds your choices. A kit update changes the manifest and never your overlay.

tour.title: A pure plan
tour.text: The plan follows from the manifest and the overlay only. It writes nothing and prints each command that changes the machine as display text.

tour.title: New directories only
tour.text: The writer creates a new, absent target or stops. The kit has no code that edits an existing profile.

tour.title: The launcher file
tour.text: The launcher starts Pi with PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR set to the target. A profile is a directory, not a sandbox.

tour.title: The live profile is refused
tour.text: The kit refuses a target in the live profile. baseline and check-baseline show any change of it.

tour.title: Validate
tour.text: validate checks the overlay against the manifest offline. A refusal prints rule: field and never a value.

tour.title: Gaps, not promises
tour.text: The kit cannot prove offline that Pi loads a package or that a model replies. It lists each such fact as a readiness gap.

tour.title: Your stages
tour.text: You install Node, Pi and the packages, you log in, and you launch. The kit runs none of these commands.

tour.title: Update by comparison
tour.text: An update is a new candidate from the same overlay. compare shows the drift, and carry prints the overlay patches.

tour.title: Core is always on
tour.text: Each other component is optional. You move its id from selection.disable to selection.enable in the overlay.

tour.title: The gateway route
tour.text: codex-accounts sends model requests to an HTTPS gateway. The key stays in the launching shell.

tour.title: Memory needs consent
tour.text: Hermes, LLM Wiki and OpenViking need consent.memoryCapture. OpenViking also needs consent.remoteMemoryWrites.

tour.title: The publish check
tour.text: Each tracked file is published, excluded or development-only. The public reader rules keep private content out of the snapshot.

tour.title: A reviewed snapshot
tour.text: publish_portable.py builds the snapshot from a clean HEAD, with only the publish set, and tags it portable/<yyyymmdd>-<sha>.

tour.title: Services stay outside the kit
tour.text: The gateway, the memory servers and the host tools are services of your host. The kit writes references, never a key.

tour.title: The Compose seat
tour.text: The same profile in a container that you reach over SSH. Not qualified.
